004.evidence: The school symbol lies south of a road junction, immediately east of a watercourse. The nearby western tributary junction and the downstream sequence of two eastern tributaries identify the corridor in the modern water network.
004.contradictions: Highway 19 supplies the previously omitted north-south through-road context. The earlier statement that the through-road is now farther south was based on an incomplete road layer and is withdrawn. The northern draft is clipped; differences in the junction cannot alone prove realignment or locate the school.
004.next: Check a dated school record or historical aerial image for the building site within this corridor.

005.evidence: The forge mark lies east of the old road, between two eastern tributaries entering the north-south watercourse above the coastal inlet. That tributary order and inlet relationship remain recognizable in NSTDB. Highway 19 now appears along the corresponding north-south road corridor.
005.contradictions: The earlier claim that the road segment was absent is withdrawn: the separate Highways layer was missing. Highway 19 is present in the corrected reference. Inlet detail differs; exact forge placement still needs site-specific evidence.
005.next: Seek an old aerial or forge-specific record; use the two tributaries to constrain the search.

008.evidence: The stables mark lies on the east side of the elongated inlet, west of the coastal road and between two eastern tributaries. The inlet, southern tributary mouth and offshore island sequence corroborate the locality. Highway 19, now included and labelled, is the essential through-road reference along this shore.
008.contradictions: The initial vector comparison omitted Highway 19. With the highway restored, the through-road corridor is recognizable; local curve and shoreline differences do not by themselves establish a change or identify a stable footprint.
008.next: Compare the road corridor with a dated aerial or stage-route record; keep Shop and P.O. associations separate.

015.evidence: The church symbol lies south of a small coastal brook and north of Rory Chisholm's Brook. The two brooks, coastline and southern inlet constrain the district. The parish's own history provides a candidate institutional identity, St. Andrew's. Restored Highway 19 follows the same broad north-south corridor beside the church search area. Janette MacDonald's 1968 St. Francis Xavier history explicitly places the present stone church where its predecessor stood, supporting reuse of the church site.
015.contradictions: The previous claim that the modern through-road lies farther west is withdrawn: Highway 19 was omitted from the reference. The historical account supports the same site but supplies no foundation plan or dimensions. Accounts disagree on completion of the wooden predecessor: MacDonald gives 1879; the Participaper gives 1860.
015.next: Compare a pre-1919 photograph or church plan with the present building to resolve the footprint; investigate the conflicting wooden-church completion dates.

external_sources.finding: Two wooden churches preceded the present sandstone church; page does not establish continuity of footprint.

external_sources.source_role: 1968 local history by Janette MacDonald, submitted to St. Francis Xavier University; digitized excerpt preserved by Library and Archives Canada
external_sources.finding: Explicitly places the stone church where its predecessor stood. Records the 1919 lightning fire, cornerstone on Dominion Day 1924, and consecration in August 1927. Supports site continuity, not identical foundations.

external_sources.source_role: contemporary newspaper construction report, The Casket, August 27, 1925, page 5; reprinted from Glace Bay Gazette
external_sources.finding: Reports Father Ronald McDonald building a Gothic church at Judique with hand-cut native stone and a planned copper roof. Confirms construction context, not the predecessor footprint.

Places the replacement wooden church farther from the shore, with a new graveyard, and gives completion in 1860; this conflicts with MacDonald's 1879 date. Reports the 1919 fire and 1924-1927 stone replacement.

021.evidence: The printed mill group lies by Rory Chisholm's Brook at the diagonal road crossing, with the large southward bend downstream and Graham River farther south. The modern brook's bend sequence and road approach corroborate this locality.
021.contradictions: Multiple small marks prevent selecting one mill building. The modern road follows a different approach north of the brook. This is separate from the southern Chisholm Brook mill group.
021.next: Resolve the mill group using a plan, aerial or site-specific historical evidence before selecting an individual feature.

077.evidence: The label is near the southern end of a north-south lane beside the northeast-southwest stream corridor, northeast of the other two mill groups. The upstream bend, small northern tributary and western road approach distinguish the locality in NSTDB.
077.contradictions: The label alone is not a building or dam point. This corridor is in the Chisholm Brook area; the pilot does not assign the main-channel name to every branch.
077.next: Resolve any printed facility mark, then check historical or local evidence for a mill or dam at this corridor.

078.evidence: The western Mills label sits at the road-and-stream crossing near a pronounced road bend, west of the eastern Mills cluster. The stream branch order and separate eastern crossing corroborate this part of the catchment. A September 1, 1892 newspaper account names mills of Alex. Chisholm and Donald Chisholm on the river behind Long Point. This is a district-level identification lead for the southern mill group; neither name is assigned to Mill B.
078.contradictions: Plural lettering and several nearby building marks do not identify a single facility or exact dam. Road and stream linework differ locally.
078.next: Search historical mill, directory or land records for Alex. Chisholm and Donald Chisholm at Long Point, then distinguish their locations among the separate mill annotations and any associated waterworks.

external_sources.source_role: contemporary newspaper account, The Antigonish Casket, September 1, 1892, page 1, Lights and Shadows of Early Settlement in Judique; scan visually checked
external_sources.finding: Names mills of Alex. Chisholm and Donald Chisholm on the river behind Long Point. Does not provide bank, footprint, mill type or a correspondence with Fletcher annotations 077, 078 or 079. The historic river description has not been independently resolved to a modern named watercourse.

079.evidence: The eastern Mills label is beside a north-south road crossing and building cluster, between the western Mills crossing and the northeastern Mill locality. The two stream corridors and road approaches are recognizable in modern NSTDB.
079.contradictions: Several buildings, a pale enclosed area and branching linework make the precise facility association unresolved. A modern crossing is not proof of the historical mill footprint.
079.next: Identify the historical building group and inspect a dated aerial or mill plan for the crossing and waterworks.

061.evidence: The Gold Mine annotation is north of the east-west road, near a tributary crossing, west of the Quartzite Mill annotation and main valley. The modern east-west road and tributary arrangement narrow the district.
061.contradictions: Geological linework overlaps the mine annotation. A place-name or nearby mineral occurrence cannot establish an opening at the printed symbol.
061.next: Find a dated mine description or plan that links the printed mark to the Melford occurrence and shaft candidates.

094.evidence: A distinct oval mine mark is west of the curving road and Glendale Brook. The brook's western tributaries and its downstream meeting with the eastern stream corroborate the corridor. Local review (September 6, 2026): the user explicitly identified annotation 094 as the gold-mine candidate that looks right.
094.contradictions: The lettering centre is well east of the reviewed mine mark. The modern road curve differs locally. The nearby GPS-sourced opening supports further investigation but does not independently establish the historical identity.
094.next: Find a dated mining account or plan linking the Glendale Brook shaft to the Fletcher annotation.

local_review.source_role: user visual review of the pilot comparison
local_review.assessment: The displayed gold-mine candidate looks right; the reviewer explicitly identified annotation 094.
local_review.scope: Visual corroboration of the candidate locality; no opening coordinates or building footprint supplied.

103.evidence: The Plumbago Mine mark lies west of the main valley and railway, south of McPherson's Brook and north of another eastern-flowing tributary. The two tributaries and eastern valley constrain a search district.
103.contradictions: No persistent access path or precise mine opening can be identified from the modern road/water reference alone.
103.next: Find the original graphite-pit description or prospect plan to establish whether GLM-1-001 is the historical Plumbago Mine.

117.evidence: The Red Bridge annotation is associated with the road crossing of the main river, west of the railway crossing. The river's northeast-to-southwest reach and upstream branch junction constrain the crossing corridor.
117.contradictions: The label centre is east of the printed crossing. The corrected reference includes the separate highway and bridge layers. Present crossings still need a dated bridge or road record before one can be identified as Red Bridge; the earlier assertion of changed road/rail relationships is not established by the incomplete comparison.
117.next: Check dated bridge or road plans to establish the former crossing and the name Red Bridge.
